key_definitions.Economics: Concerned with the study of economic issues arising because resources are scarce and have alternative uses.
key_definitions.Microeconomics: Branch of economics dealing with economic issues at the level of an individual — person, firm, industry.
key_definitions.Macroeconomics: Branch of economics dealing with the behaviour of the economy as a whole — national income, employment, price level.
key_definitions.Positive Economics: Confined to cause-and-effect relationship — states 'what is'. Based on facts.
key_definitions.Normative Economics: Concerned with 'what ought to be'. Passes value judgements. Based on opinions.
key_definitions.PPF: Production Possibility Frontier — a curve showing alternative production combinations of two goods with given resources.
key_definitions.Opportunity Cost: The cost of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made.
key_definitions.MOC: Marginal Opportunity Cost — MOC = Loss in Good Y / Gain in Good X.
key_definitions.Utility: Satisfaction derived from consumption of goods and services.
key_definitions.Marginal Utility: Additional utility derived from consumption of one more unit. MU = TU_n – TU_(n-1).
key_definitions.Consumer's Equilibrium: State where a consumer maximises satisfaction with given resources.
key_definitions.Indifference Curve: Graphical representation of combinations of two commodities giving same level of satisfaction.
key_definitions.MRS: Marginal Rate of Substitution — rate at which consumer substitutes one good for another on an IC. MRS = ΔY/ΔX.
key_definitions.Price Elasticity of Demand: Degree of responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price. E_d = (% ΔQd) / (% ΔP).
key_definitions.Total Product (TP): Sum total of output produced by all units of variable factor. TP = AP × L.
key_definitions.Marginal Product (MP): Addition to TP by employing one more unit of variable factor. MP = TP_n – TP_(n-1).
key_definitions.GDP_MP: Market value of all final goods and services produced within domestic territory in a year.
key_definitions.National Income: NNP at Factor Cost — sum total of factor incomes earned by normal residents during a year.
key_definitions.MPC: Marginal Propensity to Consume = ΔC/ΔY. Always between 0 and 1.
key_definitions.MPS: Marginal Propensity to Save = ΔS/ΔY. MPC + MPS = 1.
key_definitions.Investment Multiplier: k = 1/MPS = 1/(1–MPC). Shows multiple increase in income due to increase in investment.
key_definitions.Government Budget: Annual statement of government's expected receipts and expenditures for the financial year (1 April to 31 March).
key_definitions.Fiscal Deficit: Excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings. = Borrowings.
key_definitions.Revenue Deficit: Excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
key_definitions.Balance of Payments (BoP): Systematic record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and rest of the world.
key_definitions.Foreign Exchange Rate: Rate at which one unit of domestic currency is exchanged for units of foreign currency.

important_formulas.Percentage_change_method: E_d = (% change in Qty) / (% change in Price)
important_formulas.Income_method: NNP_FC = Wages + Rent + Interest + Profit + Mixed Income + NFIA
important_formulas.Value_added_method: GVA_MP = Sales + Change in Stock – Intermediate Cost
important_formulas.Consumption_function: C = f(Y), where C = consumption, Y = income
important_formulas.AD: AD = C + I (two-sector), AD = C + I + G + (X-M) (open economy)

key_facts_for_mcq.Perfectly_elastic_demand_curve: Horizontal line (parallel to X-axis), E_d = infinity
key_facts_for_mcq.Repo_rate: Rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks
key_facts_for_mcq.Reverse_Repo_rate: Rate at which RBI borrows from commercial banks
key_facts_for_mcq.Fiscal_deficit_means: Total Expenditure – Total Receipts excluding Borrowings = Borrowings
key_facts_for_mcq.Current_account_BoP: Trade in goods and services, unilateral transfers

numerical_question_bank.note: Numerical questions appear mainly in VSA (3 marks) and SA (6 marks). Key areas: National Income calculations, Elasticity of demand, MPC/MPS, Investment Multiplier, Cost calculations.

questions.q: When the price of a commodity decreases from ₹5 per unit to ₹4 per unit, its demand increases from 100 units to 110 units. Calculate elasticity of demand.
questions.solution:
Original price (P) = ₹5, New Price (P₁) = ₹4, ΔP = –1
Original demand (Q) = 100, New Demand (Q₁) = 110, ΔQ = 10
E_d = (–) (ΔQ/ΔP) × (P/Q) = (–) (10/–1) × (5/100) = (–)(–10) × 0.05 = 0.5
E_d = 0.5 (Less than unitary elastic demand)

questions.q: Following data is related to an economy. Calculate national income. Items: Wages ₹10,000, Rent ₹5,000, Interest ₹500, Dividend ₹3,000, Mixed Income ₹500, Net Factor Income from Abroad ₹1,000 crore.
questions.solution:
NNP_FC (National Income) = Wages + Rent + Interest + Dividend + Mixed Income + NFIA
= 10,000 + 5,000 + 500 + 3,000 + 500 + 1,000
= ₹20,000 crore

questions.q: If National Income (Y) increases by ₹100 crores and National Consumption (C) increases by ₹80 crores, find: (i) MPC (ii) MPS (iii) Investment Multiplier.
questions.solution:
MPC = ΔC/ΔY = 80/100 = 0.8
MPS = 1 – MPC = 1 – 0.8 = 0.2
Investment Multiplier (k) = 1/MPS = 1/0.2 = 5

tips: MCQ Q1-Q10 and VSA Q11-Q18 and SA Q19-Q24 are ALL compulsory — do not leave any blank
Only Q25, Q26, Q27 have OR — choose the easier option during reading time
In MCQ: CBQ (Statement I/II) questions — read both statements carefully. Usually one is positive, one is normative
Key MCQ facts to memorise: Father of Economics = Adam Smith; Father of Macroeconomics = Keynes; Elasticity = Marshall; IC Analysis = Hicks and Allen
For numericqals: MPC + MPS = 1; Multiplier k = 1/MPS; E_d formula = (–)(ΔQ/ΔP)×(P/Q)
Diagram rules: Always label X-axis, Y-axis, curves (D, S, IC, MR, MC etc.) and equilibrium point. Use a pencil first then trace with pen
For VSA 1½+1½ type: Give clearly separated 2-point answers. Use keywords the examiner expects
TR, AR, MR question — explain both under perfect competition AND monopoly for full marks
National Income numericals: Identify method (income/expenditure/value-added), list formula, substitute step-by-step
Law of Variable Proportions: Always draw BOTH TP and MP curves and show all 3 stages — examiner checks for this
Keynesian Theory: Always contrast with Classical theory for better marks. Mention 'effective demand' explicitly
Balance of Payments: Remember — Remittances by workers abroad = Current Account (NOT Capital Account). Foreign Investment = Capital Account
Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure – (Total Receipts – Borrowings). Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit – Interest Payments
Before submitting: verify roll number on both answer book and map sheets if any
